sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards appear to be suppressing near-term churn on the rules and ai_judgment tracks: both show `buffered_holdings=3`, exit streaks of 1 on MEGP.L, AEP.L, and BREE.L, `last_run.trade_count=0`, and `trades_last_7d.total=0` with `adjacent_flip_count=0` and no `duplicate_day_skip`. Cost drag is much lower on the primary ai_judgment track (`cost_drag=0.0291`, `trade_count=5`) than on the rules control (`cost_drag=0.1071`, `trade_count=23`), and rules just started a fresh knob epoch after raising `min_conviction` to 0.45. Momentum_grace is an outlier: same guard settings but `buffered_holdings=0`, `last_run.trade_count=5`, and `trades_last_7d.total=5` (all buys), so guard effectiveness is uneven across tracks. The single biggest operational learning gap is whether churn guards plus conviction floors actually close the rules-track cost-drag gap versus ai_judgment — rules still carries a watch alert at 10.7% drag while `learning_tracks_review` shows primary `excess_after_costs=-0.0506` and verdict `underperforming` despite beating the control.

sections.proposed_experiments:
1. [paper_churn] Rules track `exit_confirm_screens` 2→3 counterfactual on MEGP.L/AEP.L/BREE.L exit streaks — expected learning value: quantify whether an extra confirm screen would have blocked historical sells that drove `cost_drag=0.1071` without waiting for the new `min_conviction=0.45` epoch to mature.

2. [paper_churn] Cross-track `min_rebalance_notional_gbp` sweep (10→15→20) on momentum_grace rebalance log — expected learning value: explain why momentum_grace executed 5 buys with zero buffered holds while rules/ai_judgment held 3 names at streak=1 with zero 7-day trades.

3. [offline_sim] Rules rebalance-log replay with `exit_confirm_screens=2` vs `3` and `reentry_cooldown_screens=1` vs `2` — expected learning value: isolate guard-only cost-drag delta against the existing counterfactual baseline (`simulated_cost_drag=0.0676`, `cost_drag_delta_vs_actual=0.0395`) before any further conviction-floor moves.
